hypothesis: The parent's density-weight "damp toward 1 early" is a blunt instrument — it uniformly weakens the density gradient in the first 50 iterations regardless of whether overflow is actually rising. Instead, I gate the relaxation on *observed* overflow: only let the density weight relax (clamp to 0.5*LOWER_PCOF) when the current overflow is not above the previous one, so that when cells are being pushed into congested regions (overflow rising) the density pressure is allowed to grow normally and clear the congestion, while in the steady/freeing regime it keeps the wirelength-friendly relaxation. This preserves the parent's TNS gains but reduces the congestion-driven detours that later cost TNS.
expected_effect: TNS improves modestly (+2–6%) on bp/bp_fe, roughly neutral on ariane133; WNS neutral to slightly better; overflow stays at or below the parent's ~80–108 level; runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: gating density relaxation on observed overflow improved all three cases (score +0.160 to +0.214, all valid). Gains concentrate in TNS (up to +28.1%) with WNS also positive, consistent with reduced congestion-driven detours. Ariane133 and bp show the largest TNS moves; bp_fe smaller but still positive. Mechanism: allowing density pressure to grow when overflow rises clears congestion earlier, preserving wirelength-friendly relaxation otherwise. Next step: sweep the relaxation factor (0.5×LOWER_PCOF) and the overflow comparison window to test robustness and find the best trade-off.
